title: useRef Simulation (Stable Identity Across Renders)
problemStatement: Implement `createRefContainer(initialValue)` that returns `{ current: initialValue }` whose reference identity remains strictly constant across all calls.
interviewTrap: Thinking updating a ref re-renders the component. If UI needs to visually update on change, you MUST use `useState`.

testCases.name: Returns stable object reference across calls
testCases.testFn: const hook = createRefContainer(0); const r1 = hook(); const r2 = hook(); return r1 === r2;

testCases.name: Allows synchronous mutation of current property
testCases.testFn: const hook = createRefContainer('initial'); const r = hook(); r.current = 42; return hook().current;

testCases.name: Holds non-primitive object or DOM node reference
testCases.testFn: const hook = createRefContainer(null); const r = hook(); r.current = { tagName: 'DIV' }; return hook().current.tagName;

detailedExplanation.conceptualOverview: `useRef(initial)` returns a plain JS object `{ current: initial }` that is guaranteed to be the exact same object reference on every render. Mutating `ref.current = value` is completely synchronous and NEVER triggers a component re-render.
stepByStepWalkthrough: 1. Render Phase: Fiber node evaluation and hooks linked-list dispatch for Mutable Container Object Pattern.
2. Reconciliation: Double buffering and fiber diffing mechanics.
3. Commit Phase: Synchronous/passive effect execution and DOM mutation.
detailedExplanation.underlyingEngineInternals: In React Fiber, Mutable Container Object Pattern maintains state across work-in-progress trees and lanes scheduling priority.

complexity.time: O(1) per hook / O(N) fiber traversal

interviewCrossQuestions.question: What is the difference between useRef and useState?
interviewCrossQuestions.answer: `useState` stores state that participates in the render cycle: updating state schedules a re-render. `useRef` returns a plain mutable object `{ current: value }` whose reference identity is preserved across renders: mutating `.current` does NOT trigger a re-render. Refs are used for accessing DOM elements or storing mutable values that do not affect UI rendering.

realWorldUseCases.description: Storing timer IDs (`setInterval`) or previous prop snapshots without causing re-renders.

howToExplain.opening: useRef provides a persistent mutable container whose mutation does not trigger re-renders, ideal for DOM nodes and instance variables.
keyPoints: Returns { current: initialValue } with stable reference identity.
Mutating .current does not trigger component re-renders.
Binds to real DOM elements via ref={myRef}.
Acts like an instance variable in functional components.
howToExplain.closingImpression: useRef is the bridge between React's declarative world and imperative browser APIs.
analogies: A sticky note on your monitor: you can erase and rewrite notes on it all day without turning off and rebooting your computer.

commonMistakes.mistake: Reading or writing ref.current during the component render phase.
commonMistakes.why: Breaks pure rendering rules and produces unpredictable results in Concurrent Mode.
commonMistakes.correct: Mutate refs in useEffect, useLayoutEffect, or event handlers.

followUpDeepDive.question: How does React attach host DOM elements to refs during the commit phase?
followUpDeepDive.answer: In `ReactFiberCommitWork.js`, React sets `ref.current = hostDOMNode` during `commitMutationEffects` when mounting, and sets `ref.current = null` when unmounting.
